problem_statement: What is the infimum of |{x in R : |f(x)| < 1}| over all nonconstant monic polynomials f such that all of its roots are real and contained in [-1,1]? (Canonical source: DeepMind formal-conjectures Erdos1038.parts.i, citing erdosproblems.com/1038 and Tao25 blog post.)

feature_1_zero_curve.justification: The sublevel-set boundary {V_mu(x) = 0} is a direct analog of EHP114's lemniscate {|p(z)| = 1}, with F(x; mu) = V_mu(x) playing the role of EHP114's F(z) = |p(z)|^2 - 1. For finite atom-plus-cloud configurations the zero-set is a finite set of real boundary points {a_i, b_i}; for the continuous limit it is two intervals (primary well at +1, secondary well near -1). The codimension story matches when mu is treated as a deformation parameter.

feature_2_wall_separation.justification: The boundary-derivative signs (V_mu'(a_i) < 0, V_mu'(b_i) > 0) are observed numerically and required for the EL derivation, giving bounded-away |V_mu'(x_b)| at boundaries. However, the sublevel-measure functional exhibits non-smoothness from boundary components merging/splitting under perturbation (ERDOS1038_PHYSICS_MORPHISMS_PREPRINT.md line 71), which is the same failure family as EHP114 wall-separation failure but parametric (along mu) rather than purely spatial (along x). The recent variational-boundary-kernel robustness audit (2026-05-08) shows the brittleness-vs-bluntness tradeoff that the EHP114 center-strip cancellation was designed to handle. Failure mode is mechanical, not architectural.

feature_3_branch_point_ivt.justification: Spatial-direction interval IVT for V_mu(x_b) is tractable: V_mu is real-analytic in x away from supp(mu), and the log kernel admits a standard interval-arithmetic recipe. Bounded-away |V_mu'(x_b)| is observed at O(0.1 - 1) and the Cauchy-kernel V_mu'(x) = integral (x-t)^{-1} dmu(t) is interval-certifiable. The PARTIAL grade reflects that the EHP114 gate is really validating branch points along the parameter direction, which for #1038 corresponds to critical (w, delta) where components merge/split. The gate machinery ports cleanly, but the box is 2D parametric instead of 1D spatial, a quantitative scale-up rather than a qualitative obstruction. Pre-requisite: interval-arithmetic V_mu and V_mu' implementation (does not currently exist locally).

recommended_next_step: Proceed to B2 + B3 cold test on #1038 with three pre-condition gates: (1) interval-arithmetic V_mu kernel reaching 1e-8 enclosure width on recovered N=120 / N=200 configurations; (2) parametric wall-separation gate over a 2D box around (w*, delta*) ~ (0.174, 0.200) using interval-IVT + bounded-away |V_mu'|; (3) cold test against a non-extremal control measure (uniform or arcsine on [-1,1]) which should fail the gate or show visibly weaker margins. Pivot only if gate (1) cannot reach 1e-8 enclosure.
alternative_rationale: Primary fallback #20 (sunflower / Szemeredi): discrete combinatorial extremal with Razborov-style approximation lemma giving an explicit wall between extremal and non-extremal configurations, avoiding the continuum measure-theoretic merge/split failure mode. Secondary fallback #233 (KvN): scoped to live H2 KvN infrastructure (RPQEC / Model-Mayhem KvN runners) with operator-spectral wall-separation analog that bypasses the parametric merge/split issue entirely.
